questions.question_text: When did the Constitution of India come into official effect?
options: A) 15 August 1947
B) 26 January 1950
C) 2 October 1869
D) 26 November 1949
questions.correct_answer: B) 26 January 1950
questions.detailed_explanation: The Indian Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, celebrated annually as Republic Day.

questions.question_text: Gir National Park in Gujarat is the exclusive natural sanctuary for the endangered _____ lion.
questions.correct_answer: Asiatic
questions.detailed_explanation: Gir Forest in Gujarat is the sole remaining natural habitat of Asiatic lions in the world.

questions.question_text: Which national festival is celebrated on 26 January to mark the adoption of the Indian Constitution?
options: A) Independence Day
B) Republic Day
C) Gandhi Jayanti
D) Constitution Night
questions.correct_answer: B) Republic Day
questions.detailed_explanation: Republic Day on 26 January commemorates the enforcement of the Indian Constitution in 1950.

questions.question_text: The ancient Indian philosophy meaning 'the world is one family' is Vasudhaiva _____.
questions.correct_answer: Kutumbakam
questions.detailed_explanation: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam translates to 'the world is one big family', expressing global unity.

questions.question_text: How many regional official languages are displayed on the language panel on the back of Indian currency notes?
options: A) 5 languages
B) 10 languages
C) 15 languages
D) 28 languages
questions.correct_answer: C) 15 languages
questions.detailed_explanation: Indian currency notes feature a dedicated language panel displaying banknote values in 15 regional official languages.

questions.question_text: Traditional regional headgear styles across Indian states include turbans, topis, and _____.
questions.correct_answer: phetas
questions.detailed_explanation: Phetas (traditional Maharashtrian turbans), topis, and regional turbans reflect India's rich attire diversity.

questions.question_text: What environmental responsibility does Article 51A of the Indian Constitution assign to every citizen?
questions.correct_answer: Article 51A lists Fundamental Duties, mandating that every citizen protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife.
questions.detailed_explanation: Under Article 51A, environmental protection and compassion for living creatures are explicit Fundamental Duties of citizenship.

questions.question_text: How do Indian currency notes physically reflect the nation's linguistic unity in diversity?
options: A) They display photos of 28 state capitals.
B) The language panel on the back displays the note value written in 15 official regional languages.
C) Each note is printed in a different country.
D) Notes contain gold thread from every river.
questions.correct_answer: B) The language panel on the back displays the note value written in 15 official regional languages.
questions.detailed_explanation: Currency notes feature a language panel displaying the denomination in 15 regional scripts alongside Hindi and English.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution?
options: A) Rights protect individual freedoms guaranteed by law, while Duties represent moral responsibilities every citizen owes to the nation and environment.
B) Rights are for adults only, while Duties are for children.
C) Rights apply in summer, while Duties apply in winter.
D) There is no difference.
questions.correct_answer: A) Rights protect individual freedoms guaranteed by law, while Duties represent moral responsibilities every citizen owes to the nation and environment.
questions.detailed_explanation: Rights guarantee freedoms and equality, while Article 51A duties obligate citizens to protect national integrity and nature.

questions.question_text: How do traditional regional headgear styles like turbans and phetas reflect geographic adaptation?
questions.correct_answer: Desert turbans protect wearers from intense sun heat and sandstorms, while mountain caps provide thermal insulation against cold winds.
questions.detailed_explanation: Traditional attire evolved to meet practical climatic demands while expressing regional cultural identity.

questions.question_text: In which state is Gir Forest National Park located?
options: A) Rajasthan
B) Gujarat
C) Madhya Pradesh
D) Maharashtra
questions.correct_answer: B) Gujarat
questions.detailed_explanation: Gir National Park is located in Kathiawar peninsula, Gujarat.

questions.question_text: Article 51A of the Constitution states that protecting forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife is a _____ Duty of every citizen.
questions.correct_answer: Fundamental
questions.detailed_explanation: Article 51A specifies the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens toward natural resource conservation.

questions.question_text: What is the historical significance of 15 August 1947 compared to 26 January 1950?
questions.correct_answer: 15 August 1947 marks Independence Day (freedom from British rule), while 26 January 1950 marks Republic Day (adoption of the Indian Constitution).
questions.detailed_explanation: Independence Day marks political freedom; Republic Day marks establishing a constitutional democratic republic.

questions.question_text: How did local Maldhari pastoralist communities assist forest officials in saving Asiatic lions from extinction in Gir?
questions.correct_answer: Maldharis lived alongside lions, reported poachers, shared water sources, and tolerated livestock loss, creating a community co-existence model.
questions.detailed_explanation: Conservation succeeds when indigenous communities co-exist peacefully with wildlife and protect natural habitats.

questions.question_text: How does the ancient Indian philosophy 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' align with modern global conservation policy?
options: A) It claims only one country owns all natural resources.
B) It views the whole world as one family, emphasizing that climate systems, air, and wildlife cross all national borders.
C) It teaches that humans should conquer and industrialize all forests.
D) It prohibits trade between different states.
questions.correct_answer: B) It views the whole world as one family, emphasizing that climate systems, air, and wildlife cross all national borders.
questions.detailed_explanation: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam ('the world is one family') fosters universal empathy and global environmental responsibility.

questions.question_text: Analyze why environmental protection was included as a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A rather than just a government department task.
questions.correct_answer: Because environmental health requires daily civic habits and public participation from every citizen, not just government enforcement.
questions.detailed_explanation: Individual choices (waste disposal, water use, tree care) collectively determine national ecological sustainability.

questions.question_text: Which ecological principle explains why protecting top predators like the Asiatic lion in Gir Forest preserves the entire forest ecosystem?
options: A) Lions control herbivore populations (deer/antelope), preventing overgrazing and maintaining forest vegetation health.
B) Lions plant new trees every day.
C) Lions bring rain clouds to Gujarat.
D) Lions dig water wells for trees.
questions.correct_answer: A) Lions control herbivore populations (deer/antelope), preventing overgrazing and maintaining forest vegetation health.
questions.detailed_explanation: Apex predators regulate herbivore numbers, preventing overgrazing and protecting forest biodiversity (trophic cascade).

questions.question_text: Co-existence between local Maldhari herders and Asiatic lions in Gir demonstrates a successful community-backed _____ model.
questions.correct_answer: conservation
questions.detailed_explanation: Community-based conservation balances local human livelihoods with wildlife habitat protection.

questions.question_text: How do national symbols like the tricolour flag, national emblem, and currency notes foster national unity across diverse states?
questions.correct_answer: They serve as shared visual identifiers that connect citizens of all regional languages, religions, and cultures under one sovereign identity.
questions.detailed_explanation: National symbols represent shared constitutional values, history, and collective identity.

questions.question_text: Which action best demonstrates fulfilling the Fundamental Duty under Article 51A in daily life?
options: A) Segregating household waste, planting native trees, and conserving tap water
B) Throwing plastic wrappers out of train windows
C) Carving names onto historic monument walls
D) Wasting electricity in empty rooms
questions.correct_answer: A) Segregating household waste, planting native trees, and conserving tap water
questions.detailed_explanation: Practicing waste segregation, tree care, and resource conservation directly fulfills Article 51A duties.
